 Braves Sign Evan Phillips To Three-Year Deal
 By Steve Adams |
 at November 12, 2026 2:05pm CDT 
 The Braves have made their first significant splash of the offseason, announcing Thursday that they’ve signed right-hander Evan Phillips to a three-year, $35MM contract. The Apex Baseball client will be paid $11MM in 2027 and 2028 before earning $13MM in 2029.
 Phillips, now 32 years old, returns to the organization that originally drafted him in the 17th round back in 2015. He made a brief major league debut with Atlanta in 2018, pitching 6 1/3 innings, before being traded to Baltimore alongside Bruce Zimmerman and Brett Cumberland in the deal that brought Kevin Gausman and Darren O’Day to Atlanta.
 Phillips spent three years as a depth arm in the Orioles’ bullpen, shuffling between Triple-A Norfolk and Baltimore a dozen times before being released. The Rays signed Phillips to a minor league deal and gave him all of three innings before designating him for assignment. The Dodgers swooped in at that point, claiming Phillips off waivers, and the rest is history.
 From 2022-25, Phillips was an absolute powerhouse in the Los Angeles bullpen. He pitched 184 2/3 regular season innings and logged a minuscule 2.14 ERA with a 29.6% strikeout rate, 6.6% walk rate and 43.3% ground-ball rate. He spent time both as a setup man and closer in that window, compiling 36 holds and 45 saves — converting on 90% of the opportunities he received along the way. Phillips sat 96.2 mph on his heater in that time. His opponents averaged an awful 86.7 mph off the bat with just a 33.5% hard-hit rate in that time. His ERA over that period ranked sixth among 253 qualified relieves.
 Phillips looked to be on a collision course with a massive free agent contract until his trajectory was derailed by 2025 Tommy John surgery. The Dodgers non-tendered Phillips last winter, but L.A. brass thought highly enough of the righty to eventually re-sign him on a one-year, $6.5MM contract. They made that commitment despite the fact that Phillips would come with a 110% luxury hit and would be sidelined into July at the earliest — a testament to just how strongly L.A. brass believed in him as a potential difference maker.
 Early on, Phillips’ return was shaky. He yielded runs in five of his first seven appearances. Phillips slowly began to right the ship, however, and he was practically untouchable down the stretch. Over his final 15 innings, he allowed only three runs on nine hits and three walks — all while punching out 21 of the 57 hitters he faced (36.8%). He followed that with three more shutout innings of relief in the postseason.
 Since landing with the Dodgers via that fateful waiver claim, Phillips has quietly been one of MLB’s very best relievers. He has a 2.31 ERA in 210 2/3 innings dating back to 2022, and that doesn’t even include 18 1/3 innings of scoreless relief spread across five postseason pushes. Phillips has 47 saves and 49 holds during his regular season career, plus a playoff save and four more holds during postseason play. Whenever he’s been healthy in the past five years, he’s been a flat-out elite reliever.
 Phillips heads to an Atlanta ‘pen that looks to be in the process of experiencing some turnover. Raisel Iglesias has spent the past five years closing games for the Braves, but he’s a free agent now. It’s possible he could re-sign on a one-year deal, but Atlanta is now paying Phillips $11MM in 2027 and also has Robert Suarez signed for $16MM. They certainly have the ability to bring in another eight-figure reliever, but the Phillips addition makes it tougher to see Iglesias returning for what would be a sixth season in Atlanta.
 Whether it’s Phillips or Suarez closing games, that pair will be entrusted with high-leverage options in Walt Weiss’ bullpen. Left-hander Dylan Lee , who’s among the sport’s most underrated bullpen arms, will also factor into that mix. Fellow southpaws Dylan Dodd and Ray Kerr are also in line to pitch meaningful innings, particularly after the latter broke through as a postseason star during Atlanta’s run to the NLDS. Between veteran Reynaldo López and young Didier Fuentes , the Braves have a pair of talented righties who could function as either a critical setup arm or a mid-rotation starter. Time will tell which role each ultimately claims.
